content.title: Borders, Radius, and Shadows
content.hook: Borders, radius, and shadows can all change how an element feels, but they are not the same thing.
goals: Use borders, border radius, and box shadows to create clear visual edges and surfaces while understanding that each property solves a different problem.

content.question: You want sharp corners instead of rounded corners. Which declaration should change?

feedback.correct: Corner shape is the direct responsibility of border-radius.
feedback.incorrect: Corner shape is the direct responsibility of border-radius.

content.question: You want the card to have a visible edge even when the shadow is removed. Which property provides that edge?

feedback.correct: A border is an actual edge around the box. A shadow is a visual effect outside it.
feedback.incorrect: A border is an actual edge around the box. A shadow is a visual effect outside it.

hints.text: One declaration controls each visual effect.

content.title: Keep the job separate
content.text: Do not use a shadow to solve an actual spacing problem. Do not use a border to solve a typography problem. The property should match the symptom.

content.question: A card has the right size and spacing, but its corners are too round. What is the first property you inspect?

feedback.correct: Start with the property that directly describes the visible problem.
feedback.incorrect: Start with the property that directly describes the visible problem.
